# ISF Types, Enums, And Aggregates

This chapter is the review surface for the shipped `.isf` type, enum, and
aggregate subset. It describes what authors may write today, what the scheduled
`.fsm` review artifact preserves, and what still fails closed.

The important rule is that ISF does not own a separate type system. Local
`(types ...)` and `(enums ...)` declarations, package imports, scalar aliases,
enum members, and packed aggregate aliases reuse the same `.fsm` declaration
and package machinery that direct `.fsm` roots already use.

## Declarations And Imports

Actor-local declarations are written in the actor body. Schematic
shape (the actor body continues with `(interface ...)` and one or
more `(transaction ...)` clauses):

```text
(actor typed_actor
  (types
    (type byte (bits 8))
    (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit)))
    (type lanes_t (list bit (bits 2))))
  (enums
    (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  ...)
```

Existing `.fsm` package roots can be imported by name:

```text
(actor package_typed_actor
  (imports
    (package shared))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  ...)
```

The scheduled `.fsm` preserves these declarations as review artifacts:

```lisp
(+import shared)
(+types
  (type byte (bits 8))
  (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit))))
(+enums
  (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
```

Imported package roots are embedded into the scheduled `.fsm` output so CLI HDL
generation remains self-contained even when the lowerer uses a temporary
scheduled `.fsm` path.

## Scalar Type Aliases

Width-bearing declarations may use `(type NAME)` instead of `(width N)` when
`NAME` resolves to a scalar alias.

```lisp
(interface
  (input data (type byte))
  (output mode_out (type shared.mode_bits)))

(transaction tx
  (ports
    (input payload (type byte)))
  ...)

(storage
  (var scratch (type byte)))
```

`NAME` may be actor-local (`byte`) or package-qualified
(`shared.mode_bits`). `(width N)` and `(type NAME)` are mutually exclusive on
the same declaration. Unknown aliases fail before lowering.

## Aggregate Storage Carriers

Packed `list` and `record` aliases are accepted on actor-owned storage variables.
Packed records also support actor input ports, as described below.

Record-output declarations and exact-type whole copies are now source-admitted.
Their complete public/generated/backend execution qualification remains open.
The mandatory scheduler gate applies the qualified conservative writer rules
to each actual bound module before publishing a schedule or scheduled `.fsm`;
a multi-domain actor is checked through its separate owning domain modules.
The preparatory inventory matches each resolved output declaration to its actual
module port and joins every write to its packed range, explicit source owner
and activation conditions. A whole output overlaps each of its members;
different members may be disjoint. Repeated states of one controller and
independent controllers require different admission evidence. Equal values,
entry conditions and an empty legacy conflict report do not establish exclusion.
Local/imported nested layouts, rule/drive writers and actual domain modules are
qualified for inventory. Its private admission consumer now accepts a sole
writer or ordinary `<-` assignments in different states of one explicitly owned
transaction controller, together with disjoint physical targets. Overlapping
independent writers, duplicate writes in one active state or DT, and timed
operators have no inferred compatibility or exclusion. Caller-supplied filtered
writer lists are refused. The private inventory can inspect unresolved writer combinations; public
scheduling and emission must pass admission.
Generated output mappings remain closed until their handoff mapping is qualified. See the
[inventory evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-writer-inventory-20261001/scope.txt).
The [admission evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-admission-20261001/scope.txt)
retains the bounded rules and counterexamples. Independent-controller runtime
reachability remains governed by its separate repair and qualification tasks.

Output-only and mixed record contexts now have their mandatory preparatory
source gates. Whole copies require the same resolved record type. Scalar
samples preserve the leaf's width, signedness and state model in a private alias;
they cannot replace an existing declaration. Output record fields retain their
owning clock domain, so a read in another domain requires an explicit crossing.
The source policy keeps output member writes closed while preserving scalar
output slices and the prepared type toolkit's member facts. These checks now guard authored output declarations and whole copies; they do
not qualify output execution. See the
[source-context evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-source-contexts-20261001/scope.txt).

The shared HDL profile guard also applies to authored record outputs.
Unsupported `verilog`/`v` and `vhdl` requests name the actor, output and authored
type and recommend `systemverilog`. Mixed Verilog interfaces preserve the
existing input diagnostic priority. The old input-only helper retains its
contract, and target-neutral schedule preview stays available. Actual local,
imported, aliased, mixed and unused output sources now qualify the same normal
native/facade refusals, complete machine error products and atomic destinations.
SystemVerilog and its `sv` alias retain complete supported native HDL text apart
from date banners; these generation checks do not establish runtime support.
See the [actual target-profile evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-target-profiles-20261001/scope.txt).
See the [profile evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-hdl-profiles-20261001/scope.txt).


A whole copy can publish actor-owned storage through a declared record output:

```lisp
(actor record_output_example
 (clock clk)
 (types (type frame (record (tag (bits 2)) (payload (bits 3)))))
 (interface (input start) (output packet (type frame)) (output done))
 (storage (var held (type frame)))
 (transaction main
  (on start)
  (set held.tag 1)
  (set held.payload 5)
  (set packet held)
  (complete done)))
```

The output keeps the existing type alias and packing. Output-to-storage and
output-to-output whole copies are also permitted when their complete resolved
record types match and declared roles allow the read/write. Matching width alone
is insufficient. Scalar output-field reads and explicit scalar captures retain
the leaf's exact type. Unused record-output declarations are accepted; undriven
outputs promise no value. Typed output reset and
default options, whole-record inferred captures and root-list/formal aggregates
remain closed. Output member writes retain their separate qualification gate.
Independent overlapping output writers refuse even with equal values, different
entry guards or a priority declaration. Generated record-output mappings remain
closed until their handoff qualification. This gate applies even when the
record output is unused or the child uses only a scalar formal with the same
name. Plain local `do` without generated children remains accepted. Actual
spawned, parameterized blocking and owning-domain captures show that generated
output reads need live owner views and whole writes need an owner update route.
Both repairs precede publication; merely removing the gate would expose missing
wiring. Scalar sibling schedules can succeed while strict check and semantic
queries reject unconnected child ports. See the
[generated-output ingress](../../../docs/audits/record-output-generated-ingress-20261002/scope.txt).

The [detached child read plan](../../../docs/audits/record-output-owner-read-preparation-20261002/scope.txt)
qualifies private typed data inputs, source-name masking and emitted operand
rebasing, including record outputs named `start` and `done`. Production owner
routes and output writer handoffs remain open. Entry `when` bodies now refuse
unsupported actions rather than dropping them. First-operation conditional macro
intent and scalar X/Z false-operand diagnosis still precede read integration;
this preparation does not establish output execution or X/Z behavior.
Actual local/imported/alias/mixed,
reverse-copy and owning-domain carriers strictly replay; this establishes source
and carrier admission, with execution still pending. See the
[source-integration evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-source-admission-20261001/scope.txt).

Native check and semantic reports return the successful authored declarations in
`source.interface_ports`; schedule reports return `interface_ports` and
`clock_domains[].interface_ports` for the selected domains. Inputs precede outputs,
with authored order inside each role. Local, forward and imported aliases, mixed
interfaces, reverse copies and unused outputs retain complete layouts and types
through the in-process API and newline MCP tools. Signed and state-model facts
remain explicit; absent state models stay absent. These public products are
qualified separately from HDL execution. See the
[public-source evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-public-sources-20261001/scope.txt).

Save the example above as `.artifacts/record-output-example.isf`, then query it:

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf
./bin/fsmgen --strict --emit-semantic-json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf
./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf
```

A failed check or semantic query returns `success: false` and its contextual
diagnostic, without successful declaration metadata or a partial semantic result.
A failed schedule query publishes no schedule JSON; API/MCP retain their existing
message-only error contract. Target-profile atomic qualification and the finite complete
predecessor comparison are complete. Existing local/imported/shadowed/unused inputs,
maintained scalar/storage examples and generated/domain input sources retain their
complete public reports, strict carriers and SystemVerilog generation products.
Only qualified repository/generated-lowering directory prefixes and date banners
are normalized. [Comparison evidence](../../../docs/audits/record-output-predecessors-20261002/scope.txt)
retains the full responses and failed capture controls. The maintained
`isf/record_output.isf` now supplies a nested record/list input/storage/output
example with signed/state metadata, a whole output copy and a scalar output-field
read. Its `feature.isf_record_output` supported-smoke owner covers bounded source,
reports, lowering and SystemVerilog generation. T2037 independently qualifies
literal declaration/type/layout and corrupt-data refusal. Complete predecessor/
current catalog, all query cohort applicability and native/API/newline discovery
are retained in the [corpus receipt](../../../docs/audits/record-output-corpus-20261002/scope.txt).
Only the new entry and derived accounting change; all prior source hashes and
metadata remain exact. This does not claim actual execution of every cohort row.
Generated output mappings, field writes and execution remain separately gated.


```lisp
(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t))
  (var lanes (type shared.lanes_t)))
```

The scheduled `.fsm` keeps the authored alias in typed `+size` review entries,
and schedule reports expose the storage item with its packed `width`, authored
`type`, and resolved `type_kind` (`record` or `list`).

Packed record actor inputs are admitted with `(input NAME (type T))`, where
`T` is a local or package-qualified alias. Fields are live scalar reads in
supported transaction conditions, `set`/`update` RHS values, rules and drives.
Nested record members, list items and scalar slices use the existing packed
layout. The first authored member occupies the most significant bits.

```lisp
(actor record_input
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (signed (four_state (bits 5)))))))
 (interface (input start) (input packet (type frame))
  (output seen (width 5)) (output done))
 (storage (var held (type frame)))
 (transaction main
  (on start)
  (set held packet)
  (set seen packet.data)
  (complete done)))
```

The maintained example is [record_input.isf](../../../isf/record_input.isf).
Run `./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json isf/record_input.isf` from the repository root.

That example uses a local alias to an imported record. Its companion
[record_input_types.fsm](../../../isf/record_input_types.fsm) declares the package:

```lisp
(?pkg:record_input_types
  (+types
    (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (signed (four_state (bits 5))))))))
```

The actor imports it and retains its local spelling:

```lisp
(imports (package record_input_types))
(types (type frame record_input_types.frame))
```

Local aliases and nested members may reference declared imported types. Imports
resolve before local aliases; qualified names remain in their package namespace.
Forward local aliases also work. Missing types and undeclared packages refuse.
The scheduled carrier embeds the package root for independent strict replay.
T2014 qualifies accepted nested/imported/nearest-shadow public sources; T2015
qualifies scalar and nested imported dependencies. T2016 qualifies contextual
public refusals. T2017 qualifies the unchanged supplied SPECFORGE whole-copy and
field-guard sources, the exact earlier storage-only products and complete public
discovery. The supplied [whole-copy source](../../../docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/record-port.isf)
uses a sixteen-bit input: subtype occupies bits 15 through 12, payload bits 11
through 0. Its [field guard](../../../docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/record-port-field-guard.isf)
reads that same layout. Frontend and generated/domain source, report and replay
qualification is complete. Supported input backend and binary execution profiles
are qualified below; complete output-dependent consumer delivery remains open.

Generated readers retain one typed packed input in their private interface.
Reused instances receive the live actor input independently; an unread inherited
input is omitted from the child while the authored top declaration remains.
An input-to-storage copy keeps the register and its reset in the actor or domain
owner. A sole generated writer supplies typed private write data and an explicit
enable to that owner. Carrier checks establish structure and strict replay; the
separate direct/generated observations below qualify their timing and reset behavior.

The runnable [record_input_children.isf](../../../isf/record_input_children.isf)
imports the same package and reuses a reader in domain `io`:

```lisp
(transaction worker (domain io)
  (ports (output result (width 5)))
  (wait 2)
  (set result packet.data)
  (complete done))
(transaction main (domain io)
  (on start)
  (set held packet)
  (spawn worker as left (bind (output result seen)))
  (spawn worker as right (bind (output result again)))
  (await_all done)
  (complete done))
```

Run `./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json isf/record_input_children.isf`.
Its explicit top exposes the declared inputs and outputs, plus each domain's
clock and declared reset. `unused` stays in clock-only domain `idle`; `packet`,
`held` and the readers belong to `io`. There is no implicit crossing or child
register copy. T2019 independently qualifies local/imported nested aliases,
reused readers, unused inputs and sole generated copies, including blocking
calls. Ordinary composition children now retain their source's embedded package
context through the normal frontend; external children still resolve packages
beside their own source. T2020 checks both boundaries.

Accepted generated/domain check, semantic and schedule queries are also
qualified through the native CLI, adapter API and actual newline MCP. The
complete products agree, including declared layouts and reset provenance.
Clock-only siblings retain an absent reset; each realized reader keeps its
owning clock and explicit reset contract. Contextual generated/domain refusals
and prior-product closure are also qualified by T2021 and the execution reconciliation.

The semantic report distinguishes authored declarations from realized wiring:

| Public location | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source.interface_ports` | Authored record aliases, scalar leaf layout and declared domains. |
| `semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.signal_analysis` | The composition top's physical vector pins. |
| `semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.composition_children[].intent_hir.signal_analysis` | Each module's typed input/output declarations, including `declared_type_name` and the complete `declared_type_spec`. |
| `semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.composition_children[].structural_rtl_ir.ports` | The corresponding typed structural ports. |
| Schedule `clock_domains[].interface_ports` | The declarations owned by each domain, including unused inputs. |

Join children using `instance_name`, `module_name` and `source_name`. Reused
readers have distinct instance identities and retain the same declared type.
Private write-data ports carry the target's complete record type. Their presence
does not add authored public pins or permit competing writers.

`packet` is one six-bit input; it does not become separate field pins.
`packet.flag` occupies bit 5 and `packet.data` bits 4 through 0. The copy into
`held` requires the same resolved recursive record type. Equivalent local or
imported aliases may have different spellings; equal packed width alone is
insufficient. Member names/order, nested shape, scalar kinds, signed properties
and declared state models must match. An unspecified state model stays
unspecified for this comparison. Existing storage-only copies keep their prior
contract.

Use `(sample packet.data as captured)` in an already supported sample position
when a snapshot is needed. The private scalar alias retains the leaf width,
signed/state properties and existing capture timing. It adds no public port or
implicit reset. Alias collisions, shared transaction writers and invalid sample
paths refuse. Repeated captures by one owner preserve their existing rules.

Inputs cannot be assignment targets. Unknown members, out-of-range items,
subaggregate scalar operands, whole-record conditions/arithmetic and whole-record
sampling refuse. A nearest scalar formal or drive parameter masks an outer
record. A scalar drive parameter cannot read or write record members, even
while its width is unresolved, including member access after a scalar selector.
Bare scalar values and scalar slices keep their
existing width validation; enum/package names retain their namespace meaning. Named-domain
reads and copies require the declared owning domain or a supported crossing.
Generated child scalar outputs still require their published explicit bindings.
Strict width checks require width-aligned scalar assignments.

A static bit or slice of a named-drive scalar parameter follows that parameter,
including inside an expression. It does not read a same-named actor record.
The existing bare-parameter assignment supplies the parameter width; a selector
alone does not borrow a wider outer declaration. For example, `whole` establishes
the five-bit parameter below, while `seen` receives its low four bits:

```lisp
(actor scalar_drive_selectors
 (clock clk)
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (bits 5)))))
 (interface (input start) (input value (width 5)) (input packet (type frame))
  (output whole (width 5)) (output seen (width 4)) (output done))
 (drive (publish packet) (whole packet) (seen packet[3:0]))
 (transaction main (on start) (drive publish value) (complete done)))
```

The drive's `packet` is scalar and masks the actor's six-bit record. Its member
access such as `packet.data` still refuses. The same parameter identity applies
to an explicitly bound generated invocation and to the drive's owning domain.
Transaction locals retain their existing interface-name collision refusals.

A generated child's scalar formal can share an actor record input name. In a
binding, the formal name identifies the callee port; the actual value belongs
to the caller. The binding below sends `value` to the child's scalar `packet`:

```lisp
(actor scalar_record_binding
 (clock clk) (reset (rst_n async active_low))
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (bits 5)))))
 (interface (input start) (input value (width 3)) (input packet (type frame))
  (output observed (width 3)) (output done))
 (transaction worker (ports (input packet (width 3)) (output result (width 3)))
  (set result packet[2:0]) (complete done))
 (transaction main (on start)
  (spawn worker as job (bind (input packet value) (output result observed)))
  (await_all done) (complete done)))
```

The child keeps its scalar public port and selector. The actor record keeps its
own type, width and domain; no automatic record connection is added. Transaction
targets, instance labels and static parameter/domain/timing names also retain
their identity roles. Existing endpoint, width, timing and domain checks still
apply. This does not admit record input roots or field reads as binding actuals:
`(input packet actor_record)` and `(input packet (+ actor_record.data 0))` remain
refused. Bare slices are outside the existing signal/literal/list-expression
binding grammar; this repair does not introduce another binding form.

Rejected check and semantic queries retain their complete failure reports and
nullable diagnostic codes, without successful declarations or partial semantic
payloads. Schedule failure emits no schedule JSON. Its API and newline transport
retain the existing message-only error contract; the compiler diagnostic appears
in native stderr. None of these queries modifies the source or imported package.

Schedule preview reports scheduled intent before HDL realization. A later
composition wiring refusal, such as an unbound generated child output, can
therefore retain a complete schedule preview while strict check and semantic
queries refuse. Use those strict queries to qualify the realized composition;
a schedule preview alone does not prove its ports are connected.

Public report qualification checks complete JSON primitive kinds, source bytes,
named producers and fixed scalar/storage controls. Historical compatibility
comparisons permit only independently qualified additive metadata, exact source
relocation and emitted date banners. HDL execution remains separately qualified.

Record output declarations and exact-type whole copies are source-admitted
under SEM `.60.4.3.3.4.3`. Output member writes, root-list actor ports,
transaction-local aggregate ports, aggregate banks and variants remain deferred.
Bounded output public/profile/corpus reconciliation `.3.4.4` is complete.
Generated/backend execution qualification `.3.5` remains open. Whole-root and
member writes must be compared by their packed ranges and actual owners; an
empty conflict report does not establish compatibility. No implicit arbitration
is added. Output-field admission remains the next separate lane.
The compiler preserves typed
`+size`, explicit `+interface`, exact declaration metadata and private sample
carriers. Generated/domain source, carrier and complete public qualification
includes current catalog declarations, full discovery, contextual refusals and
fixed scalar/storage compatibility controls. Supported input backend profiles and
packed binary behavior are independently qualified below. Supplied output-dependent
consumer signoff remains separate work.
The direct public-pin behavioral witness is executed and qualified for both
emitted Verilog families. It checks packed layout, entry sampling, live reads,
whole-copy timing, held values, idle holds, repeated requests and asynchronous
reset/abort. Its independently authored
[source](../../../t/data/isf_record_input_runtime.isf) and
[bench](../../../t/data/isf_record_input_runtime_tb.sv) change the input around
public phase outputs. The data member is signed and five bits wide:

| Request | Entry-sampled data | Whole-copy data | Later live data | Prior held data |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First | 7 | -13 | -3 | -14 |
| Repeated | -2 | 9 | 5 | -13 |
| After reset/abort | 3 | -8 | -15 | -14 |

These independent literals distinguish each read/copy edge; outputs retain
their assigned values while idle. An actually compiled source with the same
width but an unsigned data member reaches the bench's signed-comparison
rejection. Complete original stage results, source identities, bounds and
cleanup are retained in the
[sealed observation](../../../docs/audits/record-input-direct-observation-20261001/manifest.json).
Generated/domain public-pin behavior is also qualified for the
[named-domain source](../../../t/data/isf_record_input_generated_domains_runtime.isf)
and [ordinary blocking source](../../../t/data/isf_record_input_generated_blocking_runtime.isf)
in both emitted Verilog families. Both use the table's independently literal
entry/copy/live/prior words, reuse live reader instances and give the packed
register one generated copier. Parent-owned phase outputs separate input
changes: the bench requires the copied scalar result during phase 1 before
phase 2, then checks every copied packed leaf and later live reads. Spawned
scalar bindings forward the child's retained output; the parameterized blocking
binding is valid during child completion and defaults to zero afterward.
The bench checks that distinction again at parent completion and idle.

Repeated requests, sampled/prior-held values, owning asynchronous reset/abort
and idle hold pass. The named source retains an unused clock-only sibling;
changing its input/clock and stopping/restarting that clock do not disturb
owned values. This establishes no initial-state guarantee for reset-free
hardware. The actually compiled unsigned counterexample passes its copied
result observation, then reaches the expected signed-comparison rejection.
Complete original results, source/producer identities, stage bounds and cleanup
are retained in the
[complete generated observation](../../../docs/audits/record-input-generated-observation-complete-20261001/manifest.json).

The first compile exposed an illegal typed wire containing two-state members;
the carrier now preserves the same packed typedef on a variable declaration.
A subsequent blocking test used the wrong late-retention expectation; its
completion-window correction preserves all packed-storage predicates. Both
diagnoses, exact predecessor controls and original partial receipts remain
tracked. SEM `.60.4.3.2.5.4.4` completes generated execution reconciliation:
current public reports, contextual refusals, package integration and prior
scalar/domain-storage contracts pass, with complete typed native/API/newline
products and unchanged source/producers. Backend profiles `.5.5.1` retain the
precise VHDL refusals below. Final public/corpus reconciliation `.5.5.2` qualifies
supplied sources, complete discovery, current catalog and JSON kinds, preserving
the unchanged full-cohort and prior evidence. Independent input signoff
`.5.5.3.2.3` closes the selected input portions of R1–R3 against their exact
source, public, profile and original native evidence. Record-output execution and
field writers, complete SPECFORGE aggregate delivery, X/Z behavior and historical
native causality remain separate obligations.

Record-input HDL support is qualified separately for each backend. The direct,
generated and named-domain witnesses above execute in both Verilog families.
The VHDL scaffold refuses these record-input profiles: the mixed signed/two-state
fixture identifies an unsupported packed member, the supplied whole-copy and
field-guard fixtures identify their typed input declaration, and the generated
tops identify their unsupported composition shape. Failure returns no successful
pipeline product, creates no new HDL destination and preserves an existing one.
Scalar VHDL inputs and the previously supported inferred packed-output fixtures
remain supported. Their file emission does not establish VHDL analyzer or runtime
qualification; see [the backend boundary](14l-backends-validation-and-apis.md).

For example, this supplied input is accepted by the frontend but its VHDL
generation refuses the typed `lmp_in` input:

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --strict --quiet --language vhdl --output .artifacts/record-input.vhd docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/record-port.isf
```

Use `systemverilog` for the qualified record-input HDL profile. HDL requests for these ISF record inputs now refuse `verilog` and its `v` alias,
naming the actor, input and declared type and recommending `systemverilog`.
They preserve an existing destination and publish no new or partial HDL product.
Source parsing, declaration metadata and schedule preview remain target-neutral.
The historical `verilog` emitter observation retained packed SystemVerilog
typedefs in these fixtures. The
record-input behavior observations compiled both emitter options as `.sv`
sources with Verilator's default SystemVerilog parser. They establish those
recorded binary behaviors, but do not qualify IEEE 1364 Verilog-2005 syntax.
The [version-matched Verilator contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/verilator/verilator/v5.050/docs/guide/exe_verilator.rst)
defines the default parser and separate language selectors. SEM `.5.5.3.2.2`
qualifies the precise current profile refusal and preserves complete SystemVerilog
HDL against the predecessor apart from date banners. The historical two-emitter
native archives remain immutable. Current T2024/T2025 preparation targets
SystemVerilog; any new native execution requires fresh observer qualification.
T2027 retains
the precise CLI/public-pipeline refusals, destination preservation, supported
controls and false-success/wrong-diagnostic counterexamples.

Run the authored source checks from the repository root:

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json t/data/isf_record_input_generated_domains_runtime.isf
./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json t/data/isf_record_input_generated_blocking_runtime.isf
```
Binary-valued Verilator execution does not establish four-state X/Z behavior;
signed/state declarations and execution claims are qualified separately.
See [0113](../../../docs/decisions/0113-isf-record-interface-ports-reuse-packed-type-and-writer-contracts.md#authored-record-input-admission--2026-09-30)
and [declared interface metadata](13a-actor-interface.md#declared-interface-metadata).
Existing declaration-collision refusals still apply.

Single-member records and single-item lists also preserve their aggregate
identity. Nested forms and forward local aliases work in actor declarations
and survive the scheduled `.fsm` replay. For example:

```lisp
(actor single_payload
  (types
    (type payload_t (list (record (payload byte_t))))
    (type byte_t (bits 8)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input data (width 8))
    (output result (width 8)))
  (storage (var value (type payload_t) (reset 0)))
  (transaction main
    (on start)
    (set value data)
    (set result value)))
```

Here the storage keeps its nested list/record shape while whole-value transfers
use the packed representation. Empty aggregates, missing member types,
duplicate field names, unknown aliases, and dependency cycles fail during type
resolution. Generated transaction children in ordinary/single-domain actors
read these same owner-held values through typed internal connections; they do
not allocate private copies. Whole-value reads use the packed representation,
and scalar leaf reads retain their exact leaf width. For example:

```lisp
(actor aggregate_child_read
  (clock clk) (reset (rst_n async active_low))
  (types (type status_t (record (payload (bits 7)) (flag bit))))
  (interface (input start) (input data (width 8))
             (output observed (width 7)) (output done))
  (storage (var status (type status_t) (reset 0)))
  (transaction worker
    (ports (output result (width 7)))
    (wait 4) (set result status.payload) (complete done))
  (transaction parent
    (on start)
    (spawn worker as w0 (bind (output result observed)))
    (wait 1) (set status data)
    (await_all done) (complete done)))
```

The worker observes the owner's later payload value. The public ports stay
scalar; the generated child receives the aggregate root with its type intact.
See [Composition](13f-composition.md) for reset ownership, live-read timing and
the remaining domain/write boundaries.

## Enum Values

Enum members may be local, such as `mode.BUSY`, or package-qualified, such as
`shared.mode.BUSY`. The parser resolves them before lowering in static
specialization contexts and preserves authored tokens in review contexts where
the scheduled `.fsm` can carry them directly.

### Enum names are not type aliases

An `(enums (NAME ...))` declaration establishes only the enum member-value
family `NAME`. It does **not** also establish a scalar type alias named
`NAME`. Writing `(type NAME)` on a width-bearing interface port, transaction
port, or storage variable when only `(enums (NAME ...))` is declared fails
closed:

```text
(actor enum_not_a_type
  (enums (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output state_out (type mode))   ;; <-- ERROR: unknown type 'mode'
    (output done))
  ...)
```

> `Error: actor 'enum_not_a_type' interface port 'state_out' references
> unknown type 'mode'`

To use an enum name as a width-bearing type, **co-declare a backing scalar
type alias** `(types (type NAME (bits k)))` alongside `(enums (NAME ...))`.
Co-declaring the same `NAME` in both `(types ...)` and `(enums ...)` is
accepted and is the intended mechanism — they are distinct declaration roles
(the `(type)` provides the width alias used by `(type NAME)`; the `(enums)`
provides the member values used by `mode.BUSY`-style references), so this is
not a redeclaration conflict:

```lisp
(actor enum_with_type
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (types (type mode (bits 1)))
  (enums (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output state_out (type mode))
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (complete done)))
```

The backing `(bits k)` width is the author's assertion and is **not**
cross-validated against enum member magnitudes — `(type mode (bits 1))` is
accepted even with a member value that needs more bits. A downstream emitter
recovering a dense `0..N-1` enum should choose `k = ceil(log2(member_count))`.

Actor-local `(types ...)`, `(enums ...)`, and `(constants ...)` declarations
need **not** be referenced to be contract-valid: an unreferenced declaration
lowers cleanly and is preserved in the corresponding scheduled `.fsm` review
section.

## Aggregate Leaf Values

Aggregate member and item paths are valid only when the root is a declared
actor-owned aggregate storage variable and the path resolves to a scalar leaf.

```lisp
(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t))
  (var lanes (type lanes_t)))
```

Valid scalar leaves include record members such as `frame.flag` and list items
such as `lanes[1]`. Unknown record members,
out-of-range list indexes, malformed paths, and paths that resolve to a whole
record/list fail before lowering.

| Context | ISF example | Lowered/reported behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transaction `set` RHS scalar value | `(set mode_out frame.mode)` | Authored aggregate leaf is preserved in the scheduled assignment. |
| Transaction `set` RHS expression operand | `(set mode_out (+ frame.mode mode_in))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |
| Transaction `set` target | `(set frame.flag flag_in)` | Scalar aggregate leaf is a writable storage leaf target. |
| Standalone transaction `when`/`while`/`until` condition | `(when frame.flag (set fire 1))` | Direct aggregate condition lowers through computed selector syntax such as `?(frame.flag)`. |
| Transaction condition expression operand | `(when (& ready frame.flag) (set fire 1))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |
| Transaction `switch` selector | `(switch frame.mode (1 (set seen 1)))` | Selector lowers through computed selector syntax such as `?(frame.mode)`. |
| Transaction `switch` branch value | `(switch mode_in (frame.mode (set seen 1)))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar branch value. |
| Rule assignment RHS scalar value | `(rule expose ready (set mode_out frame.mode))` | Authored aggregate leaf is preserved under the guarded rule DT. |
| Rule assignment RHS expression operand | `(rule expose ready (set mode_out (+ frame.mode mode_in)))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |
| Rule assignment target | `(rule capture ready (set frame.mode mode_in))` | Scalar aggregate leaf is a writable rule target. |
| Rule guard expression operand | `(rule fire (& ready frame.flag) (set seen 1))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar guard operand. |
| Standalone rule guard | `(rule fire frame.flag (set seen 1))` | Guard lowers as a non-state DT header suffix such as `<frame.flag`. |
| Named drive body RHS scalar value | `(drive publish (mode_out frame.mode))` | Authored aggregate leaf is preserved in the drive DT assignment. |
| Named drive body RHS expression operand | `(drive publish (mode_out (+ frame.mode mode_in)))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |
| Named drive body target | `(drive capture (frame.mode mode_in))` | Scalar aggregate leaf is a writable drive target. |
| Inline drive RHS scalar value | `(drive publish (mode_out frame.mode))` in a transaction body | Authored aggregate leaf is preserved in the generated state assignment. |
| Inline drive RHS expression operand | `(drive publish (mode_out (+ frame.mode mode_in)))` in a transaction body | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |
| Inline drive target | `(drive capture (frame.mode mode_in))` in a transaction body | Scalar aggregate leaf is a writable inline-drive target. |
| Named drive-call scalar actual | `(drive publish frame.mode)` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar drive actual. |
| Named drive-call expression operand | `(drive publish (+ frame.mode mode_in))` | Aggregate leaf is valid as a scalar operand. |

Aggregate paths in expression operator position remain rejected. Subaggregate
operands, subaggregate updates, whole-record/whole-list truthiness, record-output member writes and root-list
interface ports, transaction-local aggregate ports, aggregate storage banks,
aggregate field/slice/update lowering beyond scalar leaves, and broader shape
inference remain backlog.

## Diagnostics

The parser resolves type aliases, enum members, and aggregate paths before
scheduled `.fsm` emission. That means these failures are reported in ISF space:

- Unknown local or package type aliases.
- `(width ...)` and `(type ...)` on the same declaration.
- Aggregate aliases on unsupported carriers.
- Unknown enum families or enum members.
- Enum references in unsupported contexts, including operator position or LHS
  target position.
- Unknown aggregate record members.
- Out-of-range aggregate list indexes.
- Aggregate paths that resolve to whole records or lists where a scalar leaf is
  required.
- Aggregate paths outside the shipped scalar leaf contexts listed above.

Strict HDL generation is part of the shipped contract for the listed forms.

When a form is accepted, the scheduled `.fsm` review artifact is the source of
truth for how the ISF syntax reached the backend.

## Aggregate Package Constants Fail Closed

A qualified imported package constant `pkg.NAME` works only when
`NAME` is a scalar entry. Aggregate or member paths
(`pkg.AGG.member`, `pkg.LIST.idx`, etc.) fail closed across every
shipped consumer with a `remains deferred` diagnostic naming the
consumer axis. The rejected source shape is a package whose
constant is an aggregate, paired with an actor that reaches into a
member path:

```text
;; in a sibling shared.fsm file:
(?pkg:shared
  (+constants
    (CONFIG ((lat 4) (depth 8)))))

;; in the actor:
(transaction worker
  (on start)
  (wait shared.CONFIG.lat)        ;; <-- aggregate/member path
  (complete done))
```

The validator emits
`Transaction 'worker': wait count package constant 'shared.CONFIG'
aggregate/member path 'shared.CONFIG.lat' remains deferred; wait
counts accept only qualified package scalar constants in this
slice`. The same `remains deferred` phrase fires from the matching
axis-specific helper for repeat counts, latency bounds, watchdog
limits, contract windows, data-operation widths, activation
parameter overrides, actor parameter defaults, and transaction
parameter defaults. The deferred lane is aggregate/member-path
resolution against the constant-symbol table; until it ships,
authors must pre-resolve the member to a scalar `pkg.CONSTANT` (for
example `(+constants (CONFIG_LAT 4))`) or use a same-transaction
constant or parameter default instead.

## Complete Accept-Path Examples

The chapter so far has shown schematic forms and table entries.
The actors below are self-contained, copy-pasteable fixtures that
each exercise one of the shipped type/enum/aggregate axes.

### Scalar type alias

```lisp
(actor type_alias_demo
  (types
    (type byte (bits 8)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input data (type byte))
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start
      (sample data as captured))
    (wait 2)
    (complete done)))
```

**Walkthrough.** `(types (type byte (bits 8)))` declares one
actor-local scalar alias `byte` resolving to an 8-bit value.
`(input data (type byte))` uses that alias in place of `(width 8)`,
which keeps the authored intent (`byte`) visible in the scheduled
`.fsm` `+size` review entries. The transaction samples the input
into local register `captured` at entry, waits two cycles, and
completes. The lowered FSM carries the alias as a typed `+size`
entry rather than a raw width.

### Local enum

```lisp
(actor enum_demo
  (enums
    (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1) (DONE 2)))
  (constants
    (DEFAULT_STATE mode.IDLE))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (wait 4)
    (complete done)))
```

**Walkthrough.** `(enums (mode ...))` declares one enum family
`mode` with three members. Enum members are addressed dot-qualified
(`mode.IDLE`, `mode.BUSY`, `mode.DONE`). `(constants (DEFAULT_STATE
mode.IDLE))` uses the enum-member token as a constant value: the
authored `mode.IDLE` is preserved in the scheduled `.fsm`
`+constants` and `actor_constants[]` entries while the resolved
integer is available internally for static comparisons and waits.
The transaction itself is the minimal on/wait/complete skeleton —
the enum only contributes review metadata in this example.

### Aggregate storage carrier

```lisp
(actor aggregate_storage_demo
  (types
    (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit))))
  (storage
    (var frame (type frame_t)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (wait 2)
    (complete done)))
```

**Walkthrough.** `(type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag
bit)))` declares a packed record alias with two members. `(storage
(var frame (type frame_t)))` declares one actor-owned scalar
storage `frame` whose width comes from the packed sum (`2 + 1 = 3`
bits). Packed record aliases are also admitted on actor input/output ports under the
bounded record-port contracts above. Output member writes, root-list actor ports
and transaction aggregate ports remain deferred. The
scheduled `.fsm` keeps the alias `frame_t` in typed `+size`
entries and the schedule report exposes the storage item with its
packed width, authored type, and resolved `type_kind` (`record`).

# ISF Shipped Feature Matrix

This chapter is the book-facing checklist for the `.isf` surface that is
currently shipped. It does not replace the detailed chapters, the live spec,
or the downstream handoff. It gives reviewers one place to confirm which
feature families are supported, where to find examples, and where the explicit
backlog boundary starts.

A feature is "shipped" here only when the source shape, scheduled `.fsm`
lowering, runtime meaning, diagnostics, reports or review artifacts, and
focused regression evidence exist. Parser acceptance alone is not a support
claim.

## Requested Extensions And Current Gaps

SPECFORGE's configuration, verification and phase-membership requests are
owned implementation work; they are not shipped capabilities yet.

| Area | Current boundary | Requested extension |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parameter-sized ports | Width references resolve to the default; an emitted HDL parameter does not make the port generic. | Preserve width dependencies through HDL and supported instance overrides. |
| Parameter constraints | Scalar parameters carry defaults without declared legal or recommended sets. | Check legal values/ranges at defaults and overrides; report constraints and advisory recommendations. |
| Optional interfaces | Zero widths are rejected; the unsupported `present` option is rejected. | Explicit presence, absent-input values and supported per-instance specialization. |
| Actor invariants | Verification checks are written inside transactions; their existing meaning is always-on. | Actor-level `assert`/`assume`/`cover`, including actors without transactions. |
| Known-value checks | `known` and `isunknown` are unsupported. | Verification-only knownness with independent X/Z behavior evidence. |
| Physical-time durations | Timing bounds use cycle counts; clocks carry signal identity without a declared rate. | Exact duration conversion against a declared frequency/period, authored-duration and derived-cycle reports, and counter-based duration waits while preserving existing cycle-count behavior. Owned by SEM `.60.1`; not shipped. |
| Named timers | Transaction watchdog expiry is an error path; named actor timers and distinct per-await limits are refused. | Concurrent actor-owned timers with start/restart/stop, ordinary expiry conditions and schedule metadata. Cycle limits are required; duration limits follow duration support. Distinct per-await watchdog limits are optional. Owned by SEM `.60.2`; not shipped. |
| Record interface ports | Local/imported packed actor record inputs, live scalar field reads and exact-type input-to-storage copies are admitted. Frontend/generated/domain source, carriers and complete public products are qualified; direct/generated binary behavior passes both emitter options with SystemVerilog parsing. Current ISF Verilog and selected VHDL profiles refuse precisely. Selected input delivery is qualified; full output-dependent consumer delivery remains open. | Record outputs and exact-type whole copies now have bounded source/carrier admission with conservative physical writer checks; bounded public source/profile/corpus products are qualified; generated/execution qualification and output member writes remain open. Root-list ports and variants are optional. The complete request is owned by SEM `.60.4` and is not finished. |
| Transaction phase groups | Membership cannot be carried as checked transaction metadata. | Checked phase/member/role facts without invented values, order or behavior. |

Unknown or malformed interface-port options are rejected in default and strict
modes through native/API/MCP queries. This validation boundary does not add
optional-port support. Declared inputs and outputs now retain their interface
roles even when unused or undriven. Output preservation adds no value assignment.
An explicitly reset output without a data writer now resets and holds under
the module hardware-reset contract. Its semantic drive family has no data-driver
blocks. Inspect realized semantic/HDL interfaces and behavior when evaluating
presence or reset semantics.

The earlier derived-width request depends on genuine generic-width support;
it is distinct from it. Exact request scopes, repair order, current
reproductions and bounded owners are recorded in
[SPECFORGE feedback response](../../SPECFORGE_FEEDBACK_RESPONSE.md), including
its current delivery status and complete unstated-reset answer. Reset omission
selects the documented legacy default; a clock-only domain means no reset,
without guaranteed initialization. No current form defers reset policy to
instantiation.

## Status Vocabulary

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `shipped` | The listed source shape has documented lowering, runtime behavior, and regression coverage. |
| `shipped bounded surface` | The named subset is shipped; nearby wider forms fail closed or remain backlog. |
| `fail-closed boundary` | FSMGen recognizes the family enough to reject unsupported forms deliberately. It is not a runtime support claim. |
| `source admitted; qualification pending` | Authoring and required value gates are implemented; the named public/carrier/runtime and consumer qualification remains open. |

Repeat-body activation matrix note: the shipped nested-repeat activation shapes
under top-level `when` and `switch` branches are described by construction, not
by an exhaustive list of spellings. The accepted context is a repeat directly
inside a top-level branch body. The accepted activation kinds are local `do`,
generated-child `do`, generated `do` with static `(params ...)`, that generated
`do` with `(bind ...)` handoffs, and that generated `do` with optional bind
handoffs plus same-domain metadata.

The lifetime rule is the same for every accepted spelling: a blocking `do` must
observe its own fresh done handoff, generated-top parameter/binding handoffs
stay scoped to that generated `do` instance, declared same-domain metadata
records ownership without adding CDC, and every pending generated-spawn done set
remains live until a later same-body `await_all` drains the exact set before
nested repeat re-entry. `await_any` remains observation-only, including prior
observations before the `do`, post-`do` observations, and second post-spawn
observations; it never replaces the mandatory final `await_all` when more than
one generated child is pending.

Within that rule, an accepted blocking `do` may run while generated spawns are
already pending, may run after a prior multi-pending `await_any` observation,
and may be followed by one or more later generated spawns before the final
drain. The documented top-level `when` and `switch` branch paths mirror each
other. Missing same-body drains, cross-domain activation without an explicit
crossing, deeper branch/loop nesting, implicit CDC, dynamic generated-child
specialization, and broader outstanding-child lifetime semantics remain
fail-closed.

Generated-child actor-to-actor and pin route support is intentionally
small. Each route uses one direct source, one direct sink, deterministic
generated handoffs, and one named drive-call cycle. Actor-to-actor route width
is either scalar one-bit or the exact matching child endpoint width. Multiple
actor-to-actor routes are accepted only when they share the same source child,
sink child, parent transaction, contiguous route segment, and matching
endpoint widths per route. Pin-ingress route width is scalar one-bit for the
scalar multi-route subset, one exact matching top-input/child-input vector
width for the one-route vector subset, or route-local exact matching
top-input/child-input widths for the same-child vector multi-route subset.
The same-child mixed pin-ingress subset accepts scalar one-bit routes and
exact-width vector routes together while preserving route-local `kind`,
`width`, and `width_source`.
Pin-egress route width is scalar one-bit for the scalar multi-route subset,
one exact matching child-output/top-output vector width for the one-route
vector subset, or route-local exact matching child-output/top-output widths
for the same-child vector multi-route subset. The same-child mixed pin-egress
subset accepts scalar one-bit routes and exact-width vector routes together
while preserving route-local `kind`, `width`, and `width_source`.
Multiple scalar pin-ingress routes are accepted only when they share one
resolved child, one parent transaction, unique top-level input pins, unique
child input endpoints, and adjacent pre-trigger drive calls; multiple
pin-egress routes are accepted only when they share one resolved child, one
parent transaction, unique child output endpoints, unique top-level output
pins, and adjacent post-event drive calls.

mux/storage, CDC/reset remapping, ready/backpressure, payload protocols,
parameterized route drive definitions, route drive-call actual arguments,

## Examples By Family

### CLI Entrypoints

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --strict isf/apb_requester.isf
./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json isf/i2c_master.isf
./bin/fsmgen --strict --outdir .artifacts/ial1/isf-build isf/spawn_parent.isf
./bin/fsmgen -l sv isf/apb_requester.isf
```

`--emit-schedule-json` reports the scheduled intent view and exits before HDL
generation. `--outdir` is the public durable-review path for multi-file
lowering, including generated-child and accepted multi-domain actors. Without
it, those handoff files stay in a repository-local transient workspace. Plain
`.isf` HDL generation lowers through scheduled `.fsm` first, then continues
through the existing HDL pipeline.

The I2C-like fixture is a bounded realistic fixture, not a full I2C protocol

### Actor, Interface, Storage, And Timing

```lisp
(actor apb_requester
  (clock clk)
  (reset (rst_n async active_low))
  (watchdog 65535)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input req_addr (width 32))
    (output done)
    (output PADDR (width 32)))
  (storage
    (var captured_addr (width 32))))
```

This is the ordinary single-clock shape. For multi-clock actors, use
`(clock-domains ...)` instead of mixing it with `(clock ...)`:

```lisp
(clock-domains
  (domain bus  (clock bus_clk) (reset bus_rst_n))
  (domain core (clock clk)     (reset rst_n) :default))
```

### Acknowledged Event CDC

```lisp
(crossings
  (event rx_done
    (from bus  rx_done_req)
    (to   core rx_done_pulse)
    (ready rx_done_ready)))
```

The source domain may request only while `rx_done_ready` is true. The
destination domain receives a pulse later, after the generated CDC child moves
the event safely across the domain boundary.

`isf/clock_domain_no_reset_event_crossing.isf` covers the acknowledged-event
schedule/report surface when both domains omit resets. The generated CDC
metadata records `SOURCE_RESET_PRESENT 0d0` and `DEST_RESET_PRESENT 0d0`, and
the HDL path emits clock-only domain modules plus a generated CDC child without
absent reset ports.

### Transaction Body

```lisp
(transaction apb_transfer
  (on start
    (sample req_addr as addr))
  (set PADDR addr)
  (drive setup)
  (await PREADY)
  (complete done)
  (latency (min 2) (max 16)))
```

The scheduled `.fsm` review artifact owns the exact cycle placement: samples
materialize at the accepted entry boundary, drive calls consume states, awaits
test the selected port, and completion pulses the authored done output.

### Transaction Ports And Bindings

```lisp
(transaction read_word
  (ports
    (input addr (width 32))
    (output data (width 32)))
  ...)

(do read_word
  (bind
    (input addr req_addr)
    (output data read_data)))

(rule launch_read ready
  (trigger read_word
    (bind
      (input addr (+ base_addr offset)))))
```

Input bindings accept scalar signals, numeric literals, exact-width literals,
and non-empty list expressions. `do` and `spawn` support input and output
bindings; rule `trigger` supports input bindings only. Successful schedule
reports expose bounded `transaction_port_bindings[]` entries rather than raw
binding internals, with `actor_endpoint_kind` classifying the authored actor
side as `signal`, `literal`, or `expression` and `binding_timing` classifying
the transfer timing as `activation_region`, `generated_live_handoff`,
`trigger_payload`, or `done_guarded`. `authored_timing_mode` reports
`snapshot`, `live`, or JSON null for no explicit timing clause.

### Stage And Bounded-Eventually Monitor

```lisp
(transaction stream_word
  (on start)
  (stage wait_ready
    (ready ready)
    (valid valid))
  (assert (monitor (within done 8)) "finish_seen")
  (complete done))
```

The shipped stage surface is a top-level ready/valid barrier. The shipped
bounded-eventually surface is the `(assert (monitor (within SIGNAL N)) ["NAME"])`
monitor, which replaced the former top-level `(contract …)` clause. The older
`(input ready)`/`(output valid)` stage spelling remains accepted as an alias,
and the valid endpoint still participates in same-target conflict checks.
Monitor windows may use positive literals, declared positive actor constants,
actor-local scalar parameter defaults, qualified imported package scalar
constants, or same-transaction scalar parameter defaults on generated child or
direct/non-generated transactions when those sources resolve to positive
integers. Direct transaction parameters are local lowering inputs for this
monitor-window value domain and are not emitted as actor-level `.fsm`
`+params`.

Broader stage-local compute, nested stages, registered-valid/skid-buffer
variants, runtime-signal or expression monitor windows, min/max windows, and
global implication forms remain backlog.

### Waits And Repeat Bodies

```lisp
(params
  (WAIT_PARAM 2))

(transaction pulse_train
  (on start)
  (repeat count
    (drive pulse 1)
    (wait WAIT_PARAM)
    (drive pulse 0)
    (update count_seen (+ count_seen 1)))
  (complete done))
```

The repeat body may use the shipped inline body clauses documented in
[Transactions](13b-transactions.md) and [Control Flow](13d-control-flow.md).

`WAIT_PARAM` is an actor parameter wait count: scalar actor parameter defaults
that resolve to non-negative integer literals lower through the same static
wait contract as literals and actor constants. Same-transaction scalar
parameter defaults use that same static wait contract in their owning
transaction and shadow actor-level static names. Qualified package scalar
constants such as `shared.WAIT_PARAM` are accepted by that same static wait
contract when they resolve to non-negative integer literals.

A plain local `(do child)` and a same-domain generated `(do child (params ...))`
(with `(bind ...)`/`(domain NAME)` when static params are present) inside a
`(repeat ...)` that sits directly in a single `(while ...)` or `(until ...)`
body, plus the same plain-local and same-domain-generated `do` at deeper branch
nesting (`when⁺ → repeat`, `switch → when⁺ → repeat`), are part of the shipped
repeat-body subset. The first loop-plus-branch repeat-body activation is also
shipped for plain local `while -> when -> repeat -> do`; generated `do`,
spawn, `until -> when`, nested `switch`, and extra loop nesting in that family
remain deferred. The basic loop-contained/deeper-nested `spawn` + same-body
drain subset and multi-pending `await_any` with a later same-body `await_all`
drain are also shipped at lowering + composition-planning level. Deeper-nested
cross-domain repeat-body `do`, cross-domain `spawn`, undrained spawn forms,
repeats reached through an additional loop ancestor, and nested `stage` or
`contract` clauses remain outside the shipped repeat-body subset. Cross-domain
generated `do`, loop-contained/deeper-nested undrained `spawn`, and
extra-loop-ancestor repeat-body `do` each emit targeted diagnostics so authors
can identify which deferred lane is
blocking their specific case; the original generic "supported only for
top-level..." message remains as a safety-net fallback.

<details>
<summary>Repeat-body construction-rule audit markers</summary>

These short markers let the feature-matrix audit detect the shipped
repeat-body activation families without restoring the old exhaustive list of
individual spelling combinations:

```text
top-level repeat-body local blocking do
samples before or after spawn before same-body sync
samples before or after repeat-body do before the repeat check
multi-pending repeat-body await_any with mandatory same-body await_all drain
documented top-level when/switch nested-repeat activation construction rule
local do, generated-child do, static params, bind handoffs, same-domain metadata
await_any observation-only plus same-body await_all exact drain
```

</details>

### Types, Enums, And Aggregate Leaves

```lisp
(types
  (type mode_bits (bits 2))
  (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (valid bit))))
(enums
  (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t)))

(transaction publish
  (on start)
  (set frame.mode mode.BUSY)
  (when frame.valid
    (set out_mode frame.mode)))
```

The shipped aggregate path is scalar-leaf based. `frame.mode` and
`frame.valid` are accepted because `frame` is declared actor-owned aggregate
storage and the paths resolve to scalar leaves.

Runtime expression divisor safety is fail-closed for literal zero, fixed actor
constants that resolve to zero, actor scalar parameters whose defaults resolve
to zero, and same-transaction scalar parameters whose defaults resolve to
zero:

```lisp
(constants (ZERO 0) (DEN 2))
(params (ZERO_P 0) (DEN_P 2))
;; inside a transaction: (params (TX_ZERO 0) (TX_DEN 2))
(set out (/ numerator divisor))  ;; accepted: dynamic divisor, no proof yet
(set out (/ numerator 8'd2))     ;; accepted: nonzero literal divisor
(set out (/ numerator DEN))      ;; accepted: nonzero actor constant divisor
(set out (/ numerator DEN_P))    ;; accepted: nonzero actor parameter divisor
(set out (/ numerator TX_DEN))   ;; accepted when TX_DEN is a nonzero same-transaction parameter
(set out (/ numerator 0))        ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator ZERO))     ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator ZERO_P))   ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator TX_ZERO))  ;; rejected when TX_ZERO resolves to zero
```

### Bank Store And Load

```lisp
(storage
  (bank data (width 8) (depth 4))
  (var wr_ptr (width 2))
  (var rd_ptr (width 2)))

(transaction fifo_step
  (on push)
  (store data wr_ptr data_in)
  (load data rd_ptr as data_out)
  (complete done))
```

The bank is scalarized in scheduled `.fsm` review text. Pointer-selected
access remains explicit through `store` and `load`; memory-array backend
emission is not a current support claim.

### Rules, Priority, And Resources

```lisp
(rule high write_req
  (set valid 1))

(rule low read_req
  (priority over high)
  (set valid 0))

(resources
  (resource rule_exec
    (kind rule_slot)
    (arbiter priority)
    (users high low)))
```

The shipped `rule_slot`/`priority`, `output_bundle`/`priority`,
`transaction_start`/`priority`, `storage_port`/`priority`, bounded
`rule_slot`/`round_robin`, bounded `output_bundle`/`round_robin`, bounded
`transaction_start`/`round_robin`, and bounded
`storage_port`/`round_robin` subsets can gate a whole bound rule DT for
one active cycle. Remaining resource kinds are documented names, not supported
runtime arbitration behavior yet.

### Generated Children

```lisp
(transaction worker
  (params
    (WIDTH 8))
  ...)

(transaction parent
  (on start)
  (spawn worker as w0
    (params
      (WIDTH 16)))
  (await_all done)
  (complete done))
```

The lowerer emits a scheduled parent `.fsm`, scheduled child `.fsm`, and a
generated top `.fsm`. The generated top applies static parameter overrides and
wires start/done handoffs.

### Reusable Library Use

```lisp
(imports
  (library common.fifo as fifo_lib))

(use fifo_lib.fifo as u_fifo
  (params
    (DATA_WIDTH 8)
    (DEPTH 4)
    (PTR_WIDTH 2)
    (OCC_WIDTH 3))
  (bind
    (clock clk)
    (reset rst_n)
    (input write_req write_req)
    (input data_in data_in)
    (output full full)
    (output data_out data_out)))
```

The cataloged `common.fifo.fifo` actor is a shipped reusable ISF library
definition. Library imports are semantic roots that still lower to scheduled
`.fsm`; they are not textual includes.

### Schedule JSON And Manifest Discovery

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json isf/apb_requester.isf
./bin/fsmgen --capability-manifest
./bin/fsmgen --emit-capability-manifest
```

The schedule report is the machine-readable companion to the scheduled `.fsm`
review artifact. The capability manifest advertises the live ISF public
contract, including this book chapter through `live_document_paths`.

```json
{

  "actor_params": [
    { "name": "WIDTH", "value": 8 }
  ],
  "actor_phases": [
    { "name": "capture", "body": [["note", "metadata"]] }
  ],
  "actor_stages": [],
  "verification_observations": [
    {
      "name": "link_rx",
      "role": "passive_monitor",
      "clock": "clk",
      "reset": { "name": "rst_n", "kind": "async", "polarity": "active_low" },
      "signals": [
        { "name": "valid", "direction": "input", "width": 1 },
        { "name": "ready", "direction": "output", "width": 1 },
        { "name": "data", "direction": "input", "width": 8 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "inferred_storage": [
    {
      "name": "wait_count",
      "kind": "counter",
      "role": "dynamic_wait_counter",
      "width": 4
    },
    {
      "name": "done_fail",
      "kind": "register",
      "role": "temporal_contract_monitor"
    },
    {
      "name": "worker_process_start",
      "kind": "register",

```

The manifest flag `schedule_report_full_schema_stable` is true for
`schema_version: 1`. Consumers should still prefer advertised keys, value
families, and explicit role fields over parsing generated signal names as
semantic API.

### Downstream Issue Bundles

```bash
./bin/fsmgen-issue-bundle \
  --case path/to/fsmgen-facing-artifact \
  --issue-id sf-0001 \
  --speforge-version "SPECFORGE_COMMIT" \
  --failure-class unknown \
  --expected "FSMGen should accept this generated artifact" \
  --observed "FSMGen rejects it" \
  -- --strict --check --json
```

Downstream tools do not need to decide whether the root cause is `.fsm`,
`.isf`, parser, lowering, HDL, or API-specific before filing. The bundle
captures the FSMGen-facing artifact, exact command, environment, observed
stdout/stderr/status, JSON probes, generated artifacts, and a rerunnable
`commands.sh` so the issue can be reproduced from the FSMGen repository root.

## Explicit Non-Claims

These are important because they prevent the matrix from implying support that
does not exist:

- Multi-bit CDC payloads, FIFO CDC, reset-as-event semantics, and direct
  cross-domain data access are not shipped.
- A cross-domain `(do CHILD)` directly inside any TOP-LEVEL body — a `(repeat ...)`
  body or a `when`/`switch`/`while`/`until` branch body — and directly inside a
  `(repeat ...)` nested in a top-level `when` body or top-level `switch` branch,
  plus directly inside supported nested `when` chains reached from those top-level
  branch bodies and repeats under those chains, IS shipped (the dual-CDC handshake
  runs when the branch is taken and re-runs each iteration inside a repeat/loop; see
  the cross-domain activation crossing row).
  Generated or spawned nested activation beyond the documented top-level
  branch-contained generated do
  cases and top-level branch-contained spawned cases, broader outstanding-child
  semantics, deeper branch repeat activation beyond the shipped top-level
  `when`/`switch` branch-contained repeat crossing, nested
  nested switch, repeat-contained branch, nested `while`, nested `until`, `stage`,
  `contract`, and DEEPER-nested cross-domain
  activation (a cross-domain `(do)` whose container is itself nested inside another
  body rather than a direct transaction-body clause) remain outside the
  shipped repeat-body subset.
- Dynamic division/modulo nonzero proof is not shipped. Literal-zero,
  actor-constant-zero, actor-parameter-zero, and
  same-transaction-parameter-zero divisors are rejected, but arbitrary runtime
  scalar divisors and nonzero use-site-specialized parameter divisors are
  emitted unchanged.
- Enum members are not writable targets, and enum members in expression
  operator position fail closed.
- Record output member writes, root-list interface ports, transaction-local aggregate
  ports, aggregate banks, subaggregate updates, and whole-record/list truthiness
  remain backlog. Whole record outputs/copies have bounded source/carrier admission
  above; packed record actor inputs have the qualified bounded admission above;
  this does not complete broader generated/domain/native or consumer delivery.
- Backlog resource kinds are registry names, not runtime arbitration support.
- Actor-level phase and stage metadata is report-only; it does not schedule
  actor-level runtime phases, barriers, generated `.fsm` states, or HDL
  behavior.
- Actor-level passive observation metadata is report-only; it does not emit
  generated `.fsm`, HDL, UVM, VHDL, scoreboard, coverage, or VIP artifacts.
  The shipped form is `(observe NAME (role passive_monitor) (signals SIG...))`
  over unique public actor interface signals in a single-clock actor.
- ATL generated-child actor-to-actor routes do not support generated-handoff
  remapping or reuse. Parent-declared collisions with selected trigger,
  event, data, or named-drive request handoff names fail closed with focused
  parser-owned coverage for normal `.isf` source and lowerer-owned coverage
  for malformed or mutated scheduler-facing actor metadata. This is not a new
  source feature. Route mux/storage, fan-in/fan-out, CDC/reset remapping,
  ready/backpressure, payload protocols, route drive parameters, route
  drive-call actual arguments, recursive actor networks, and permanent actor
  grouping also remain outside the shipped generated-child actor-to-actor
  route subset.
- Direct `(on ...)` activation-site `(params ...)` is unsupported and fails
  with an entry-guard/generated-activation diagnostic; static specialization
  belongs to spawn, generated blocking `do`, and rule-trigger generated
  activation sites.
- Rule-trigger output bindings for direct/local targets, explicit
  behavior-changing snapshot-vs-live binding timing selection/conversion,
  additional future binding-report expansions beyond the shipped bounded
  `transaction_port_bindings[]` summary fields, and broader static binding
  conflict diagnostics are not shipped. The shipped summary fields include
  `actor_signal`, `actor_expression`, endpoint kind, binding timing, and
  authored timing mode. The direct/local rule-trigger output-binding
  diagnostic names the missing generated-child completion identity. Duplicate
  output actor targets inside one bind block, and duplicate generated
  rule-trigger output actor targets inside one rule, fail closed before
  broader assignment conflict handling.
- Nested stages, stage-local compute/action bodies, multiple ready/valid
  endpoints, registered-valid variants, and skid buffers are not shipped.
- Temporal contracts beyond the top-level bounded eventual subset, including
  runtime-signal or expression windows, global implication forms, dynamic
  bounds, expression operands, and multiple outstanding obligations, are not
  shipped.
- Raw parser actor hashes, private `LoweringIR` internals, raw assignment
  provenance lists, and recursive child report dumps are not public schedule
  JSON API.
- VHDL is recognized as a target family, but the full VHDL backend is not
  shipped.

When a future slice widens any row above, update the detailed chapter, this
matrix, the live spec, the downstream handoff, the public contract or manifest
metadata when applicable, focused tests, and the feature backlog in the same
task-scoped commit.
